cards.text: It's the next day, and Jesus and His disciples are heading out of Bethany, a village near Jerusalem. And Jesus is hungry. Friend, I know hungry. I've stood at that oven door counting down the timer like it's New Year's Eve.

cards.question: Hungry Jesus spots a tree in leaf off in the distance and walks over to see if there's any fruit on it. What kind of tree is it?
When Jesus reaches the fig tree, He finds a few figs hiding under the leaves.

cards.text: Nothing but leaves, friend. Mark tells us 'it was not the season for figs.'

cards.question: Jesus finds no figs on the tree. Then He speaks to the fig tree itself. What does He say?

answers.text: No one will ever eat its fruit again
It will be full of figs by morning
It will be cut down before evening

cards.question: Jesus says this to the fig tree with nobody around to hear it.

cards.text: Hold that thought, friend. They head into Jerusalem, and Jesus walks into the temple courts, where people are buying and selling.

cards.question: People are buying and selling right there in the temple courts. What does Jesus do?

answers.text: He begins to drive them out
He sits down and watches them
He buys a dove for an offering

cards.question: As He drives them out of the temple courts, Jesus overturns the tables of the ___.

cards.text: The money changers' tables go over, and so do the seats of the dove sellers. I knocked over ONE jar of sprinkles once and was picking them out of my mustache for a WEEK.

cards.question: Jesus won't let anyone carry ___ through the temple courts.

cards.text: Then Jesus begins to teach them. He points them to what is written about God's house.

cards.question: Jesus asks if it isn't written what God's house will be called. What will it be called?

answers.text: A house of prayer for all the nations
A house of offering for the priests
A house of gold for the kings

cards.question: Jesus says God's house will be called a house of prayer for all the nations. But what does He say they've made it?

cards.text: The chief priests and scribes hear all this. These are the temple's top priests and the teachers of the law.

cards.question: After hearing Jesus in the temple courts, the chief priests and scribes start looking for a way to ___ Him.
The chief priests and scribes are afraid of Jesus because the crowd has turned against Him.

cards.text: When evening comes, Jesus and His disciples go out of the city. Big day, friend. And that fig tree is still out there.
Next morning, they're walking back. And who do they pass on the way? Our old friend, the fig tree.

cards.question: Walking back the next morning, Jesus and His disciples see the fig tree ___ from its roots.
Seeing the withered fig tree, ___ remembers what Jesus said to it and speaks up.

cards.text: Peter, one of the Twelve, says, "Look, Rabbi! The fig tree You cursed has withered." That's me with every tray out of the oven, yelling LOOK so loud the whole planet hears.

cards.question: Peter points out the withered fig tree. What does Jesus tell the disciples?

cards.text: Then Jesus paints a picture: someone telling this mountain, 'Be lifted up and thrown into the sea.' Friend, it takes me three tries to get a stuck cookie off the tray, and Jesus is talking MOUNTAINS.

cards.question: Jesus says the mountain will be thrown into the sea even if the one who says it doubts in his heart.
Jesus takes the mountain picture and brings it to prayer. When you ask for something in prayer, what does He say to do?

answers.text: Believe that you have received it
Keep asking until a sign comes

cards.text: And Jesus adds one more thing for when you stand to pray.

cards.question: When you stand to pray and hold anything against another person, what does Jesus say to do?

answers.text: Forgive it and let it go

cards.question: Jesus connects forgiving others with your Father in heaven forgiving your trespasses.

cards.text: Forgive, Jesus says, so your Father in heaven forgives you too. I got swapped for a shinier stamper and slid into a junk drawer, and friend, carrying that grudge would've been heavier than any cookie box I've ever packed.

findings.problem: The opening card has 4 sentences: "It's the next day...", "And Jesus is hungry.", "Friend, I know hungry." and "I've stood at that oven door...". The limit is 3.

rule.text: The opening card can be up to 3 sentences. It says who is speaking, to whom, and what is going on. If the passage starts in the middle of a thought, it gives the context.

findings.problem: The passage starts mid-narrative with "The next day" (Mark 11:12). The opening card never says what came the day before. Jesus had entered Jerusalem, looked around the temple, and gone out to Bethany with the Twelve (Mark 11:11). Without that, "the next day" has no context, and the temple scene later has no setup.

rule.text: If the passage starts in the middle of a thought, it gives the context.

findings.problem: The card states an outside fact, that Bethany is a village near Jerusalem (John 11:18). It gives no reference for it, and the card cites only Mark 11:12.

rule.text: Facts from outside the passage are fine when they help, like who a new person is or who wrote a letter, with their reference.

findings.problem: The card explains who the chief priests and scribes are ("the temple's top priests and the teachers of the law"). That fact comes from outside the passage, and the card gives it no reference. It cites only Mark 11:18.

rule.text: Facts from outside the passage are fine when they help, like who a new person is or who wrote a letter, with their reference.

findings.problem: The card says "Peter, one of the Twelve." That fact comes from outside the passage (Mark 3:14-16), and the card gives it no reference. It cites only Mark 11:21.

rule.text: Facts from outside the passage are fine when they help, like who a new person is or who wrote a letter, with their reference.

findings.problem: The last story card retells Mark 11:25 ("Forgive... so your Father in heaven forgives you too"). Choice cards 10 and 11 already covered that verse in full. The card is a recap and doesn't move the passage forward. The joke could ride on card 9 or be dropped.
